en: Salutations to Śrī Sundaragaṇapati. Re-31372:
The Ritual Procedure for the Consecration of the Fire-pit (Kuṇḍa).
Dots (... indicate missing portions due to leaf damage or unidentified characters;
words or letters within brackets are my suggestions based on my understanding.
Most folio sides contain seven lines.
Red color indicates possible errors;
i = image, l = line number.

(i.3b, l.1) The fruit is the size of a *bagarī* fruit. These sixty-three substances—beginning with barley and ending with the three myrobalans (*triphalā*)—are each ten in number according to their respective roots. Having performed the oblations (*homapurassaraṃ*), and having offered the *sviṣṭakṛt* sacrifice with the *havyāvāha* mantra while all the substances are combined, [one should perform] the expiation outside the enclosing sticks (*paridhi*) with water from the *sakṣālūra* vessel; inside the enclosing sticks, for the sake of atonement, five [substances] are used separately, numbering five each.

Having performed the protection of the sacrificial ground with the *varma* mantra of many forms, and having performed the self-protection (*ātmanāśa*) with the *vara* mantra, one should offer ten oblations separately according to the rule and give the final full oblation (*pūrṇāhuti*). Having presented incense, lamps, food offerings (*naivedya*), and so forth, up to the waving of the lamp (*ārātrika*), and having offered the oblations, one should pray for the supreme state. Having performed the sprinkling of water as previously described and having approached the fire, one should fix the heart [mantra] in its form and preserve the increased fire. One should also perform the fire-oblation in the Āgneya pit.
Now follows the procedure for the fire-oblation (*homa*) in the southern pit (*dakṣiṇakuṇḍa*).

Then, having caused the patron (*yajamāna*) and the officiating priests (*mūrtipa*) to sip water for purification (*ācamana*), and having seated himself upon the tortoise-throne (*kūrmasana*), he should perform the ritual of self-protection (*sakalīkaraṇa*), prepare the general offering (*sāmānyārghya*), sprinkle the pit with the weapon-mantra (*astramantra*), and after striking his head [with the hand], pray to Vighneśvara. Having performed three breath-controls (*prāṇāyāma*), he should make the formal resolve (*saṃkalpa*)... for the propitiation of the Supreme Lord (*parameśvara*) residing therein.

Having made the formal resolve (*saṃkalpa*): "I shall perform the evening *homa* in the Dakṣiṇāgni fire for the Śiva-sacrifice of the restoration of the ruins of Sadāśiva," and having purified [the materials] with water... [one performs] the five purificatory rites (*pañcasaṃskāra*) of the sacrificial pit (*kuṇḍa*). With the Sadyojāta mantra, the sprinkling (*prokṣaṇa*): *Oṃ saṃ sadyojātam*. With the Vāmadeva mantra, the scattering of soil (*avakiraṇa*): *Oṃ siṃ vāmadevāya*. With the Aghora mantra, the drying (*śoṣaṇa*): *Oṃ huṃ aghorāya namaḥ*. With the Tatpuruṣa mantra, the baking (*pācana*): *Oṃ hoṃ tatpuruṣāya namaḥ*. With the Īśāna mantra, the sprinkling (*prekṣaṇa*): *Oṃ hoṃ īśānāya namaḥ*. Having thus performed the five purificatory rites, [one proceeds] to the center of the sacrificial pit.

In the south, north, middle, west, and east, with the six mantras beginning with *brahmajñāna*, having drawn lines extending from the east to the west and from the north to the south, one should inscribe: *brahmajñānam*, *nāke suparṇam*, *āpyāyasva*, *yo rudro agnau*, *idaṃ viṣṇuḥ*, and *rudram... apipīdan*. Having thrown away the fragments and half-eaten portions of the sacrificial wood (*akṣa*), [one should join] the central line and those starting from the east. *Oṃ hāṃ*.

Salutation to Brahmā. Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Vaivasvata; oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Soma. Having worshipped [these] on the lines extending from the center toward the north, [and likewise] oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Rudra; oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Viṣṇu; oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Śakra—having thus honored them, having spread out *darbha* grass, having established the fire in the southern sacrificial pit (*dakṣiṇāgni-kuṇḍa*) from the principal pit, having sprinkled water around it and strewn grass, having gratified it with the *agnijanana* mantras and kindled it, [one recites] "devasya tvā..."

Having first strewn the sacrificial grass (*barhis*) with its tips pointing eastward, high and thickly spread, according to the mantras of the *diś* and *cakra*, and having placed the southern [fires] from north to south, he should then spread the grass to the north for the purpose of preparing the vessels.

Having placed the fuel-sticks (*samidh*) and *darbha* grass upon the southern *kāśa* grass at the place of the oblation (*homavyoni*), and having prepared the two forms of the *sruc* and *sruva* ladles, the vessel for clarified butter (*ājyasthālī*), the sprinkling-vessel (*prokṣaṇipātra*), and the water-pot (*kamaṇḍalu*) on the north—these being the pairs of implements to be employed—he should complete the preparations.

Taking the *prokṣaṇī* vessel, having placed a *kurca* [grass-bundle] therein, having filled it with water, and having arranged flowers and unbroken grains (*akṣata*) within it, one performs the sprinkling three times. Having sprinkled the vessels with that very *varman* [armor-mantra], and having made the fire-pit (*kuṇḍa*) and so forth at the time of their respective requirements, and having sprinkled them, one takes the *ājya* vessel, places the *kurca* therein, fills it with cow-products (*gavya*), and having offered oblations to the deities beginning with Aṃ Gaṃ Nā... in the western direction, one arranges two blades of *darbha* grass.

Having poured water [into the vessel], having performed the circumambulation with fire (*paryagnikaraṇa*) using two *darbha* blades and so forth, having performed the circumambulation with fire with the tips pointing northward, having moved it away toward the north, having pushed back its tip over the *darbha* grass,

and having placed it on the western side of the fire, having performed the three-fold sprinkling (*ukṣaṇa*) with the thumb and ring finger, having untied the knot, having touched water, having cast the fire [into the vessel], and having moved the ghee clockwise, one should place it upright.

Having placed another bundle of grass (*kūrca*) upon that [altar], having washed the *sruk* and *sruva* ladles with water as if they were one's own garments, and having taken them along with *kuśa* grass, one should heat them over the fire and wipe them with the tips, middles, and roots of the *darbha* blades. Having discarded the *darbhas* into the water, one should place the root-end of the *kūrca* on the left side of oneself for the purpose of purification. Then, having consecrated the *śakti* with the *Śiva-mantra* and others, and having taken the enclosing sticks (*paridhi*), one places one in the west with "Oṃ hiṃ, to the armor (*kavaca*), vauṣaṭ";

one places one in the north with "Oṃ haḥ, to the weapon (*astra*), phaṭ"; and one places one in the south with "Oṃ haṃ, to the eyes (*netra*), huṃphaṭ. Finally, one places two upright fuel-sticks (*samidh*) with "To the heart, namaḥ."

Having performed the rite with "Śirase svāhā" and having sprinkled the fire-god Pāvaka with perfumes and other offerings, one should worship: in the east on the enclosing sticks (*paridhi*), "Salutation to Brahmā"; in the south, "Salutation to Viṣṇu"; in the west, "Salutation to Rudra"; in the north, "Salutation to Ananta. Within that enclosure, "Salutation to the Eight Vasus"; outside of that, "Salutation to the Seven Maruts. Having worshipped Indra and the other world-protectors (*lokeśas*) upon the sacrificial grass (*paristaraṇa*), [one worships] in the fire:

"Salutation to Ādhāraśakti," "Salutation to Ananta," "Salutation to Dharma," "Salutation to Jñāna," "Salutation to Vairāgya," "Salutation to Aiśvarya," "Salutation to Padma," and "Salutation to the seat of Dakṣiṇāgni."

(1.5) [One should worship] the two-faced [deity] with the luster of gold, having three feet and seven hands; from the right face, he grants gold and other riches; in the three faces of the tongues beginning with Suprabhā, there is a heap of ashes, gravel, and fire; in the heart, there is rising water; in the right hand, a *tomara* (spear) and a fly-whisk (*cāmara*), and in the left, a vessel of ghee; three rams are in the southern sacrificial pit (*dakṣiṇakuṇḍa*) born of the Southern Fire; obeisance to the form of the Southern Fire (*dakṣiṇāgnimūrti*).

(i.5b, l.1) To that [deity], for the sake of the seat of the sacrificial form born from the half-portion of the Lord, ... [one] should perform [the rite] with a beautiful girdle joined to the essence of the sacrificial butter, and pay homage to the sacrificial form of Agni whose limbs are smeared with fresh butter.

(l.2) ... To its presiding lord, the arrow... one should meditate upon the three-eyed one, born from the *kūrca* grass, holding a discus, a trident, and a sword, filled with the inner essence of the serpent. One should offer oblations to the south for the presiding lord of the sacrificial form, to that Lord.

One should meditate upon Nārāyaṇa, who is seated on a lower seat, three-eyed, and adorned with a crown; likewise, he is decorated with earrings, possesses a radiant breast-ornament (*uraḥsraja*), has fangs, and a face like that of an elephant. He wears a garland of skulls, is resplendent with serpents, and holds a *duścika* and a mirror. In his four left hands, he holds a *khaṭvāṅga*, a trident, a shield, and a noose. In his four right hands, he holds a *triśūla*, an axe, a sword, and a *ṣaṇḍa* for crushing enemies. One should thus meditate upon Nārāyaṇa.

To the one who has the luster of the sun, the non-terrible, the source of all, salutation to the one whose form is non-terrible; salutation to Aghora. Having worshipped [the deity] from the invocation (*āvāhana*) up to the end of the *idupānta*, at the time of the food offering (*naivedya*), one should offer ten oblations of clarified butter with the Aghora mantra.

Then, having offered two hundred and five oblations of clarified butter with the Aghora [mantra], one should offer half of that number of oblations of parched grain (*barasvi*), parched rice (*tila*), and boiled rice (*caru*) with the Aghora [mantra];

with the Īśāna [mantra], [offer] barley (*yava*); with the Śiras [mantra], wild rice (*nāja*) and black gram (*māṣa*); with the Śikhā [mantra], one handful of parched grain (*prathagukṛta*); and with the Astra [mantra], an oblation of the size of a fresh *āmalaka* fruit.

(i.6a, l.1) With the *śiras* [mantra], one should consume a cake (*apūpa*) the size of a *sruva*; with the *netra*, a substance the size of a *sruva*; with the *īśāna*, milk; and with the *sugandha*, water the size of a *sruva*. That [mixture] is to be sprinkled with curd. (l.2) With the *vāmadeva*, [substances] the size of a *sruva*; with the *aghora*... [like] a *punnāga* fruit; with the *mūla*, a piece of sugarcane the size of a joint; with the *īśāna*, a plantain leaf; half a *phekha*.

The mango fruit, the *aliptaca* fruit, the jackfruit (*panasa*) of its own size, and the thorny fruits—having removed the stalks and the like, one should divide them into thirty parts and offer them one by one as oblations. For the *badarī* fruit, it is of its own size; for the coconut, having divided it into eight parts, one part is for a single oblation. With the root of the *ekadāga*, there are the *sūraṇa*, *bālaka*, and *badarī* fruit. The *padmakanda* and *apalakanda* are also of the size of a *badarī* fruit.

Having gone there, one should perform the *homa* with the root mantra using sandalwood, *kesara*, *karṇikāra*, *gorocana*, *agni*, *raṅka*, *krama*, the two *mṛtarābhi*s, and *candra*. Indeed, this is the *kalparañcaṇa-trahoma* for the foremost of seeds (*vijamukhya*).

[With] *hrīṃ*, *berāśiraṃ*, and *marūdamanā*, having cut these to the measure of two finger-breadths, one should perform the *homa* with *gulurumāṣa* by means of the ten-syllable mantra. One should offer flowers to the Lord of the World... with the *aghora* mantra.

One *pūlaka* of rice, one *erlava* of *kasa*-grain combined with the root-mantra, chickpeas (*caṇaka*) and so forth, half a *kadana* of *niṣpāva*, bamboo shoots (*vaiṇava*), *mudga* beans—these [should be] a mere handful; sesame, earth, and *mudrā* beans, a measure of eight *muṣṭi*s; clarified butter (*siddhājya*) and mustard seeds (*sarṣapa*), a measure of two *muṣṭi*s; *gośīrṣa* sandalwood, a measure of a *muṣṭi*; the fruit of the *badarī* tree, a measure of a *muṣṭi*; fresh turmeric, the fruit of the *jātī* jasmine, and the fruit of the *badarī* tree—a measure of a *muṣṭi*. These [are the offerings] beginning with barley and ending with the three fruits (*jātīphala*).

(1.2) Having performed ten oblations for each of the three substances with the root mantra, preceded by the *vyāhṛti* homas, and having offered eight oblations to Śiva with the mantra "Havyavāha" while joined with all six substances; (1.3) having poured the inner enclosing sticks (*paridhi*) into the fire as the outer enclosing sticks, and having offered twenty-five oblations with the five-armed [mantra] according to the number of the injunctions for expiation for all ritual errors, one should offer oblations with the *karmavarma* mantra and the *pāpadauṣa* mantra.

Having offered ten oblations for each [deity] with the sword-mantra *Śambara* while reciting the name of oneself, having duly given the *pūrṇāhuti*, having presented the *śiras-pādi* [offering], and having offered the *ārātrika* lamp, one should conclude by saying "Obeisance. Having sprinkled water around the fire (*pariṣicya*) and arisen, one should restrain Aghora residing in the fire by means of the *Bahurūpa* mantra and protect the directions from the north. The procedure for the sacrificial offering (*homavidhi*) in the right-hand sequence is completed.
Now follows the procedure for the Nirṛti-homa and the procedure for the Nirṛti-kuṇḍa.

The presiding priest of the Arka-mūrti, having performed the ritual sipping of water (ācamana), seated himself upon the tortoise-posture (kūrma-āsana), performed the ritual identification with all parts of the body (sakalīkaraṇa), and prepared the water-offering (arghya), sprinkled the sacrificial pit (kuṇḍa) with the weapon-mantra (astra-mantra), and having prayed to the Lord of Obstacles (Vighneśvara) while striking his head [with the hand], performed the three breath-restraints (prāṇāyāma). Having made the formal resolve (saṃkalpa): "For the sake of pleasing the Supreme Lord (Parameśvara), I shall perform the fire-oblation (agnihoma) for the restoration and re-binding of the old [shrine] of Sadāśiva," he [prepared] the half-pit of the sacrificial ground.

The purification by means of the five sacramental rites (*pañcasaṃskāra*) is as follows: with the *Sadyojāta* mantra, *Oṃ Haṃ Sadyojātāya Namaḥ*, [one performs] the washing (*kṣālana*) with the left; with the *Vāmadeva* mantra, *Oṃ Hiṃ Vāmadevāya Namaḥ*, [one performs] the drying (*śoṣaṇa*); with the *Aghora* mantra, *Oṃ Aghorāya Namaḥ*, [one performs] the sprinkling (*prokṣaṇa*) with the *Tatpuruṣa* mantra, *Oṃ Heṃ Tatpuruṣāya Namaḥ*; and with the *Īśāna* mantra, *Oṃ Hoṃ Īśānāya Namaḥ*. Having thus performed the five sacramental rites, [one proceeds] to the south, north, middle, and west of the sacrificial pit (*kuṇḍa*).

In the eastern [sections], having drawn six lines—three pointing eastward and three pointing northward—with mantras beginning with *brahmajñāna*, and having inscribed [the following]: *brahmajñānaṃ*, *nāke suparṇam*, *āpyāyasva*, *yo rudro*, *idaṃ viṣṇur vicakrame*, *tridhā nidadhe padam*, and *pradhīḥ*, one should discard the splinter from the edge of the sacrificial post (*akhara*) toward the northeast. Then, from the center, [one should mark] the line starting with the east: *oṃ hāṃ brahmaṇe namaḥ*; *oṃ hāṃ*...

(1.5) Homage to Vaivasvata; Oṃ Hāṃ, homage to Soma in the center and at the northern tip; Oṃ Hāṃ, homage to Rudra; Oṃ Hāṃ, homage to Viṣṇu; Oṃ Hāṃ... having performed [the rites]... from the primary *kuṇḍa* of Nirṛti, having established the fire in the *Nirṛti-kuṇḍa*, having sprinkled it around and strewn it about, and having kindled it with the *agni-viḍana* mantras, one should [proceed] with the *devasya tvā* and other mantras, and with the *stradaya* [offering] in the directions starting from the east.

Having strewn ten blades of *darbha* grass each, with their tips pointing eastward and their bases pointing northward, and having placed them so that those to the south are higher than those to the north, and those to the north are higher than those to the south... for the purpose of preparing the vessels, there should be three [blades] from the northern part... and *darbha* grasses for the two oblations; having offered the southern oblation (*dakṣiṇahuta*), one should cease. Having sprinkled water around the fire and performed the ritual attendance (*upasthāna*), and having removed the sacrificial implements and the *kūrca* grass, one should guard the fire. The procedure for the oblation in the eastern pit (*vāyukuṇḍa*) is completed. Now follows the procedure for the oblation in the northern pit (*uttarakuṇḍa*).
Now follows the procedure for the fire-oblation (*homa*) in the northern sacrificial pit (*kuṇḍa*).

Then, having seated the image of Soma upon a tortoise-throne (*kūrma-āsana*), having performed the ritual of total identification (*sakalīkaraṇa*), having honored him and offered the respectful oblation (*argha*), having protected the pit from the corners, and having prayed to Vighneśvara after first striking the ground with the head [of the ladle], one should perform three breath-controls (*prāṇāyāma*). Having made the formal resolve (*saṃkalpa*) for the sake of pleasing the Supreme Lord, [one should perform] the fire-oblation consisting solely of clarified butter in this Śiva-sacrifice for the purpose of binding the decayed joints of this Sadāśiva.
(l.4) ... having formed the mental resolve ... [performing] the purification by means of the *savana* [offering]: *oṃ haṃ sadyojātāya namaḥ*; *oṃ vān menakṣa...* [and] *hiṃ vāmadevāya* (l.5) ...
[and] *aghorāya namaḥ*; the cooking by means of *tatpuruṣa*: *oṃ haṃ tatpuruṣāya namaḥ*; the sprinkling (*prokṣa*) by means of *īśāna* (l.6) ...
having performed the consecration (*saṃskāra*), [one performs] the *brahmajijñāna* and so forth in the center, south, north, middle, lower, and eastern parts of the sacrificial pit (*kuṇḍa*).

(l.7) ...having performed the ritual preparation for the *kuṇḍa* in the middle, south, and north, and in the middle, west, and east; having [recited] "Brahmajijñāsā" etc., and having drawn the lines... [reciting] "jñānaṃ nāke suparṇam" and "āpyasva"; [reciting] "yo rudro" and "idaṃ viṣṇuḥ" (i.8a, l.1)... [reciting] "kṣya śakalam"... on the upward and eastward-pointing lines: "oṃ hāṃ brahmaṇe namaḥ", "oṃ hāṃ vaiśvānarāya..."

On the lines of the *rāgara* [mandala], having worshipped with "Oṃ Vaṃ, obeisance to Rudra; Oṃ Hāṃ, obeisance to Viṣṇu; Oṃ, obeisance to Śakra," and having spread out *darbha* grass, [one should proceed] from the principal *kuṇḍa* to the northern *kuṇḍa*. Having kindled [the fires] with half-measures of fuel, one should [draw] the lines with a cord. Then, with the verse beginning "devasya tvā" and the four [mantras] ending in "triṣṭubh," one should [place] ten *darbha* blades each in the directions starting from the east. Having performed [the rites] up to the north, for the purpose of setting out the vessels, one should turn [the materials] to the north; and the *darbhas* suitable for the *homa* are to be placed on the right side.

...just as [previously] described, [one should proceed] further: having turned face-downward the vessel for clarified butter (*ājyasthālī*), the sprinkling-vessel (*prokṣaṇapātra*), the water-pot (*kamaṇḍalu*), and the two *darvī*-ladles, and having set them aside; then, taking the sprinkling-vessel, placing a tuft of grass (*kūrca*) within it, filling it with water, and arranging flowers and unbroken rice grains (*akṣata*); having performed the ritual three times with silver, one should sprinkle the vessels with those very waters. At the time when each respective purpose arises, one should turn [the vessels] face-upward and sprinkle them thoroughly.

Taking the vessel of clarified butter (*ājyapātra*), having placed the *kurca* grass bundle therein, and having filled it with cow’s products (*gavya*), one should cast embers from the western fire onto it, place it upon them, split it at two points at the tips, touch water, and pour the clarified butter into it. Having worshipped the two ends of the *darbha* grass, and at the time of the food offering (*naivedya*), having offered ten oblations of clarified butter with the *śikhā-mantra*, one should then offer fifty-two hundred oblations of clarified butter with the *śikhā-mantra*. Then, [one should offer] with a fuel-stick of *khadira* wood...

Having offered *śālīcaru* with the *śikhā-mantra*, one should offer rice mixed with *māṣa* beans for the head with the *īśāna-mantra*; *dhyāmāka* grain and *pūryaṅgu-traliṣva* with the *śiras-mantra*. Having offered [the oblation] for the name with the *aghora-mantra*, one should offer milk-rice (*kṣīrābha-tarasa-anna*), rice with jaggery (*gulānna*), and the five grains (*pañcānna*) and so forth, in the measure of an *āmla* fruit; a cake (*apūpa*) in the measure of the head with the *pūrva-mantra*; milk-porridge (*pāyasa*) in the measure of a ladle (*sruva*) with the *īśāna-mantra*; and milk, sugarcane juice, and Ganges water.

The measure for the *sruva* spoon is as follows: curd with the *tatpuruṣa* mantra; honey with the *vāmadeva* mantra, using a *sruva* spoon as the measure; a *guñjā* berry with the *aghora* mantra; a root the size of a *puṃnāga* fruit; a piece of sugarcane the size of a *paṣa*; a plantain fruit or half a fruit with the *īśāna* mantra; an *ātma-phala*, a *likuca* fruit, and a *panasa* fruit, each according to its own natural measure; having extracted the bulbous roots (*kandaka*) and so forth, thirty [parts] for *śaṃyin*; and for a single oblation (*ekāhuti*), a single portion of the *badarī* fruit according to its own natural measure.

Having cut the coconut into eight pieces, one should perform a single oblation (*ekāhuti*) once with the root mantra. Having cut the *sūraṇa* root, the *khadarī* fruit-sized [root], the *bālaka*, the *dapatmakarda*, and the *apalakanda*—these being the size of a chickpea (*caṇakamātra*)—one should perform the oblation with the root mantra. Having ground together camphor, gorocana, *kāgniraṃtra*, *krama*, *muṭnākṣidvaya*, *caṃtra*, *vāmatoya*, and camphor, each the size of a chickpea, one should perform the oblation with the primary seed-mantras (*bījamukhya*). [The offering is made to] Śrībera and the head.

(i.9a, l.1) Having cast out these [substances] today, measuring one finger-breadth, namely: a *maṭa*, *gulgu*, *la*, and *māṣa* measure; with the ten-syllable mantra (*daśākṣara*), flowers; with the *puṃs* [mantra], the *bilva*; with the *aghora* [mantra], those three leaves; *elā*, *laṃ*, *vaṃ*; together with the *kajā*, *trīphala*, leaf, and *kāsa*; with the root-mantra (*mūla*), chickpeas (*caṇaka*); ten [of each]; *niṣpāva*; nine *ṣiṣ* [seeds]; *āghaka*; bamboo; *mutga*; these [measured] like a stalk of sugarcane; sesame; that which is brought by the *mṛgīmudrā*; *māṣa*; and a *śukṣi* measure.

Having offered *siddhārtha* (white mustard seeds) and *sarṣapa* (black mustard seeds) separately in quantities of one *muṣṭi* (handful), cow-dung the size of a *gedhnima*, a *khadarī* fruit, half a *palārdha* of fresh turmeric, and a *yadyarī* fruit; having first performed the *vyāhṛti-homa* for each of these sixty-three substances—beginning with barley and ending with the *jātīphala* fruit—ten times for each substance, and then combined them with the serpent-substances while reciting the root mantra.

Having offered the *sviṣṭakṛt* oblation with the mantra "havyāvāham," and for the sake of attaining wealth and fame, having offered ten oblations each with the five-weapon [mantra], the half-[mantra], the armor [mantra], the *bahurūpa* [mantra], the *pāpatakṣaṇa* mantra, the ninefold *ātman* [mantra], and the *śambara* [mantra], and having performed the full oblation (*pūrṇāhuti*) while reciting "pivat," one should worship with the services beginning with lamps, incense, and food offerings up to the final propitiation (*ārārtika*), and then offer the heart-oblation (*hṛta*).

(1.7) Having prayed with "parama," having sprinkled [the oblation], and having [placed] the fire near the... having restrained the one situated in the fire with the *bahurūpa* mantra, one should protect it. Thus ends the procedure for the *nirṛti*-pit offering. Now follows the procedure for the western pit offering.
(1.9b, 1.1) Now follows the procedure for the western pit offering.

Then, having sat upon a seat made of a water-image, a cloth, and a tortoise-skin, having performed the purification (*sakalīkaraṇa*), having prepared the general offering (*sāmānyārghya*), and having sprinkled the sacrificial pit (*kuṇḍa*) with the weapon-mantra (*astra-mantra*), [having worshipped] the Lord of Obstacles (*Vighneśvara*) by striking his head [with flowers], and having performed three breath-controls (*prāṇāyāma*), he should make the formal resolve (*saṅkalpa*): "For the sake of pleasing the Supreme Lord, in this Śiva-sacrifice consisting of the restoration of Sadāśiva’s temple, I shall perform the evening *āhavanīya* fire-ritual using the *gārhapatya* fire..."

They should perform the consecration of this western fire-pit (*kuṇḍa*) with the five purificatory rites (*pañcasaṃskāra*): purification by burning with *Sadyojāta*: *oṃ haṃ sadyojātāya namaḥ*; washing with *Vāmadeva*: *oṃ hiṃ vāmadevāya namaḥ*; drying with *Aghora*: *... aghorāya namaḥ*; cooking with *Tatpuruṣa*: *heṃ tatpuruṣāya namaḥ*; and sprinkling with *Īśāna*: *oṃ hoṃ īśānāya namaḥ*. Thus [is] the fivefold consecration.

In the center, south, and north of the *kuṇḍa*, having drawn three lines with their tips pointing east and north using the six mantras beginning with *brahmajajñānam*— namely, *brahmajajñānam*, *pūrṇamadaḥ*, *āpyāyasva*, *yato jyotiḥ*, *yo rudro bhūtaḥ*, and *viṣṇururukramaḥ*— and having scraped away the fragments with the *arkas* mantra, one should [place] *oṃ hāṃ brahma...* upon the lines starting from the center and extending toward the east.

(1.7) *Oṃ hāṃ vaivasvatāya namaḥ*, *oṃ hāṃ somāya namaḥ*; on the lines with their tips pointing north from the center: *oṃ hāṃ rudrāya namaḥ*, *oṃ hāṃ viṣṇave namaḥ*, *oṃ hāṃ śakrāya namaḥ*. Having thus worshipped, [and having] placed *darbha* grass...

(i.10a, 1.1) Having established the fire in the western pit from the [central] pit, having sprinkled water around it and strewn [grass] around it, having [performed] the *agnijanana* and kindled it, one should [worship] in the directions starting from the east with the *devasya tvā* and other mantras, and with the *cakrabhrama* mantras.

Having spread the grass with its tips pointing eastward and upward, and having placed the vessels from south to north and from west to east, one should strew grass for the purpose of preparing the vessels. Having strewn it to the north, one should offer fuel-sticks and *darbha* blades into the fire. To the south of the fire, [one places] the *sruk* and *sruva* ladles; to the north, the vessel for clarified butter (*ājya-sthālī*), the sprinkling vessel (*prokṣaṇī-pātra*), and the two *meḍhrī* [strainers]. Having arranged the sacrificial spoons and the *yośakhā* [wooden pieces], one takes the sprinkling vessel, places a tuft of grass (*kūrca*) within it, and...

Having placed flowers and unbroken rice (*akṣata*) and performed the sprinkling three times, one should sprinkle the vessels with that same armor-mantra (*varman*). At the time of preparing each respective [substance], having turned the face upward and sprinkled [them]...

having taken the *arghya* vessel and placed a tuft of grass (*kūrca*) within it, having filled it with cow-products (*gavya*), having suppressed the embers in the west... having arranged them and fixed two tips of *darbha* grass, having touched water and poured in clarified butter (*ghṛta*)...

Having performed the *yyagnikaraṇa* rite, having moved the vessel toward the north, having pushed its tip back, and having placed it upon *darbha* grass on the western side of the fire; having thrice raised [the ladle] with the thumb and ring finger, having made it hollow, and having released the *gṛddhi*; having cast [the fuel] into the fire, having poured clarified butter while circumambulating [it] clockwise, and having placed it upward; having placed another *kūrca* upon that [ladle], and having washed the *sruk* and *sruva* with the *astra-mantra*; having taken up those two slender [handles] and heated them over the fire, [he should touch] the tips and the middle of the *darbha* grass.

(i.10b, l.1) Having cast the *darbha* grasses into the fire with the *jya* [formula], having placed [the fuel] from the left side of oneself... having deposited the roots at the base... having fully worshipped the mantras of Śiva and Śakti and others, and having taken up the *pariyūna*, one deposits it in the west with "Oṃ hiṃ, to the armor, vauṣaṭ"; one deposits it in the north with "Oṃ haṃ, to the weapon, phaṭ"; one deposits it in the south with "Oṃ huṃ, to the eyes, huṃ phaṭ"; and one deposits it above with "To the head, svāhā. Having sprinkled [water] around and addressed the fire, one honors it from the right while [placing] the enclosing sticks (*paridhi*)...

In the east, *namaḥ* to Brahmā; in the south, *namaḥ* to Viṣṇu; in the west, *namaḥ* to Rudra; in the north, *namaḥ* to Ananta; on all sides, *namaḥ* to the eight Vasus; outside of that, *namaḥ* to the seven Maruts. Having worshipped the world-protectors, such as Bhujyu and others, upon the sacrificial grass (*paristaraṇa*), [one worships] in the fire: *namaḥ* to the power of the upward stream (*ūrdhvadhāraśakti*); *namaḥ* to Ananta; *namaḥ* to Dharma; *namaḥ* to Jñāna; *namaḥ* to Vairāgya; *namaḥ* to Aiśvarya; *namaḥ* to Padma; *namaḥ* to the seat of the Gārhapatya fire. [One worships] the red-bodied one, the red-colored...

One should meditate upon [the deity] who, with his two upper hands, holds a sacrificial ladle (*sruva*) joined with the gestures of granting boons (*varada*) and fearlessness (*abhaya*); who possesses a single face, bears matted locks (*jaṭā*), and has seven tongues of flame blazing like a string of pearls; who is seated upon a horse and is adorned with ornaments. In the fifth small enclosure (*kuṇḍaka*), one should worship the form of Arghapati; there, salutation to the one whose seat is the Water-form (*Jalamūrti*). Varuṇa, accompanied by his attendants, resides in a crocodile (*makara*); there, one should worship Jalamūrti, whose nature consists of four arms and who is adorned with all ornaments.

Salutation to him who is the presiding lord, whose seat is Rudra; salutation to the three-eyed one with four arms, wearing a crown of matted hair and adorned with all ornaments—one should meditate upon Rudra in the west. Salutation to the form of Rudra; salutation to his lord, who is seated upon the seat of Sadyojāta, who holds a deer-skin and a rosary, who wears a white turban, who is white, and whose limbs are complete in every part—one should meditate upon him in the west. Oṃ, salutation to the form of Sadyojāta; Oṃ Haṃ, salutation to Sadyojāta. [Perform] the invocation and other rites.

Having worshipped the [deities] of the directions at the time of the food offering (*naivedya*), one should offer ten oblations of clarified butter (*ājya*) with the *sadyojāta* mantra. Then, having offered two hundred and fifty oblations with the *sadyojāta* mantra, one should offer half of that number [one hundred and twenty-five] with the *riñcataru* mantra; barley with the *īśāna* mantra; rice with the *śiras* mantra; millet (*sāmāka*) and *priyaṅgu* seeds with the *śiras* mantra; and parched grain (*uddhānna*) and *mudga* beans with the *aghora* mantra.

Milk-rice, rice with sesame, rice with molasses, and rice with five ingredients—these are the five foods. A portion of mango and *āmalaka* equal to the size of the head; a portion of cake for the eyes; milk-porridge (*pāyasa*) equal to the size of a sacrificial ladle (*sruva*) for the face;

milk for Īśāna; the essence of food; and Ganges water equal to the size of a sacrificial ladle for Tatpuruṣa; curd, honey, and ghee equal to the size of a sacrificial ladle for Vāmadeva; molasses and *puṇṇāga* fruit for Aghora; and a piece of sugarcane the size of a joint for Mūla, [offered] with Īśāna.

The plantain fruit, the *ātrabala* fruit, the *likuca* fruit, and the *panasa* fruit—having set aside their own respective measures, having set aside a thirtieth part, there is one portion for each oblation; the *badarī* fruit [is offered]. The coconut, having divided it into eight parts, there is one portion for each oblation with the root-mantra. Having offered [the rest] as before, the *bālakaṇḍa*, the *padmakaṇḍa*, the *utpala-kaṇḍa*, and so forth—these are all the size of a *badarī* fruit.

(i.11b, l.1) …… taking camphor, sandalwood, kastūrī, black aloe-wood, gorocanā, and the sequence beginning with *raṅku*, the two types of musk (*mṛganābhi*), moon [white sandalwood], snow-water, *kapittha*, and *cañcanāratra*; with the primary seeds for the *homa* sacrifice, *uśīra*, and *rudraja*—having grasped these with the fingers, [along with] *tagara*, guggulu, *māṣa*, *tridaśākṣa*, …… flowers, and fruit; with the lower [part] three betel-leaves in sequence, one by one, together with *elā*, *lavaṅga*, and *putrikā*.

With *śila* [grain] from the regions of Caṇaka, with *niṣpāva* beans, with half a *vaiṇava* measure of *ārdhaka*, these being merely a handful; a *bhṛti* measure of sesame, a *mudga* bean, and a *meṣa* measure of *aguṇin* *siddhārtha* along with *saṣa*;

pure rice (*śuddhānna*) separately by a *muṣṭi* measure; wheat by a *śakti* measure; cow dung; *badarī* fruit; fresh *haritrika* vegetables; fruits of the *jāti* variety; and *bamarī* fruit by a measure—having offered these one by one with their roots.

(1.5) Having offered one, two, or up to sixty-three substances for each *āhuti*, preceded by the *homa* and separately ten times for each, having performed the *sviṣṭakṛt* offering combined with all three [mantras], and for the sake of expiation (*prāyaścitta*) for any deviation from the rite, having offered twenty-five oblations individually with the five-weapon mantra, [he offers] with the *varma* [mantra]... with the mantra for the destruction of sins and the [mantra] for the self... with the sword [mantra], ten oblations for each.

Having offered the full oblation (*pūrṇāhuti*) according to the rules, and having performed the ritual services from incense and lamps up to the food offering (*naivedya*) as prescribed in the manual, one should dissolve [the deity] and offer clarified butter (*ghṛta*). Having sprinkled the supreme water for the feet (*arghya*), one should worship the fire and, having restrained it in its true form, one should protect the fire. The procedure for the fire-oblation in the western pit is completed.
Now follows the procedure for the fire-oblation in the northern pit.

Alternatively, having sipped water for purification (*ācamana*), performed the ritual identification with the limbs (*sakalīkaraṇa*) upon the tortoise-seat (*kūrmasana*), and prepared the general offering (*sāmānyārghya*), one should sprinkle the sacrificial pit (*kuṇḍa*) with the weapon-mantra (*astra-mantra*). Having first struck the ground with the head [of the hand] and prayed to the Lord of Obstacles (*Vighneśvara*), and having performed the triple breath-control (*prāṇāyāma*), one should make the formal resolve (*saṃkalpa*) on an auspicious lunar day:

"O Supreme Lord, in this Śiva-sacrifice for the restoration and eightfold binding (*aṣṭabandhana*) of Sadāśiva’s dilapidated [shrine], I shall perform the oblation for the establishment of the young fire. Having thus resolved, the five purificatory rites (*pañcasaṃskāra*) should be performed; the cleansing is done with the *Sadyojāta* mantra.

Oṃ haṃ, obeisance to Sadyojāta; [perform] washing with the left [face]. Obeisance to Vāmadeva; [perform] drying with the lower [face]. Oṃ huṃ, obeisance to Aghora; [perform] cooking with the Tatpuruṣa [face]. Oṃ haṃ, obeisance to Tatpuruṣa. Obeisance to Īśāna; [perform] sprinkling with the Īśāna [face]. Oṃ hoṃ, obeisance to Īśāna. Having thus performed the five purificatory rites (*pañcasaṃskāra*), [one should act] in the middle, south, north, west, and east of the sacrificial pit (*kuṇḍa*).

Having drawn [the diagram] with the tips of the lines pointing eastward using the mantras beginning with *brahmajajñānam*, [and reciting] *brahmajajñānam*, *nāke suparṇam*, *āpyāyasva*, *yordudre*, *idaṃ viṣṇu*, and *viśvā avasyur...* (l. 7), having consecrated it with water and cast away the fragments, one should place [the syllables] on the lines starting from the center and extending eastward:
*oṃ hāṃ brahmaṇe namaḥ*, *oṃ hāṃ vaivasvatāya namaḥ*, *oṃ hāṃ somāya namaḥ*. On the lines starting from the center and extending northward... (incomplete).
